meanings: a question on public transport: are you getting off at the next stop?
forms: literally: do you get off at the next one?

examples.en: Excuse me, are you getting off at the next stop?

note: Used to ask someone to let you through to the door. Other questions: «Која је следећа станица?» (What is the next stop?), «Када полази следећи воз?» (When does the next train leave?).

meanings: get lost, go away (a mild euphemism for a rude phrase)
forms: literally: go to three beautiful ones

examples.sr: Остави ме на миру, [ѝди у три̏ лѐпе]!
examples.en: Leave me alone, get lost!

note: The last word is left out. A playful rhyming variant: «иди у три лепе шаргарепе». Not for formal settings, but you will hear it in films.

meanings: to put an end to, to wrap up
forms: literally: to put a period

examples.sr: Време је да [ста̀вимо та̏чку] на ту причу.
examples.en: It's time to put an end to that story.

note: Similar: «ставити питање» - to ask a question, «ставити услов» - to set a condition.

forms: literally: a minute to twelve

examples.sr: Стигао је [у мѝнӯт до два́нае̄ст], али је стигао!
examples.en: He arrived at the last second, but he made it!

examples.sr: Пријавила сам се [у мѝнӯт до два́нае̄ст].
examples.en: I registered at the very last moment.

note: Said of someone who made it in time at the very last moment.

meanings: to come to mind, to occur to someone
forms: literally: to fall onto the mind

examples.en: What were you thinking? (What came into your head?)

note: The person takes the dative, the thing that occurs is the subject.

meanings: to faint; to be in shock
forms: literally: to fall into unconsciousness

examples.sr: Пала је [у не̏све̄ст] кад је сазнала вести.
examples.en: She fainted when she heard the news.

note: Figuratively: «Пали смо у несвест после тог сусрета» - we were in shock after that meeting.

meanings: to catch the eye, to stand out
forms: literally: to fall into the eyes

examples.sr: Пао ми је [у о̏чи] овај леп шешир.
examples.en: This nice hat caught my eye.

forms: literally: to fall at an exam

examples.en: The student failed the exam.

forms: literally: to fall onto something

examples.en: I would never fall for that.

forms: literally: to go out to a meeting

examples.en: I'm going on a date with her tonight.

note: Colloquially - «дејт».

forms: literally: to be in a connection

examples.en: They have been together for a year now.

note: Colloquially - «забављати се». To break up: «раскинути»; to end a relationship: «прекинути везу с неким».

forms: literally: to hold on to each other's hands

examples.sr: Шетају парком и [др̀же̄ се за ру̀ке].
examples.en: They walk in the park holding hands.

forms: literally: to interrupt the connection

examples.sr: Одлучила је да [прѐкине ве́зӯ] са њим.
examples.en: She decided to break up with him.

note: A colloquial variant is «раскинути».

forms: literally: Michaelmas summer

examples.en: Belgrade is expecting an Indian summer.

note: Named after Михољдан, October 12. The other form is «бабље лето».

meanings: said of a person whose mood and opinions change quickly
forms: literally: changeable like autumn weather

examples.sr: Не могу да га разумем, [промѐнљив је ка̏о јѐсење вре́ме].
examples.en: I can't understand him, he's as changeable as the autumn weather.

meanings: weak autumn sun that shines but gives no warmth
forms: literally: toothed sun

examples.sr: Изашло је [зу̀бато су̑нце], али дува хладан ветар.
examples.en: The sun came out, but a cold wind is blowing.

meanings: to get soaked to the skin
forms: literally: to get drenched to bare skin

examples.sr: Нисам имао кишобран, па сам [покѝснуо до го̀ле ко̏же].
examples.en: I didn't have an umbrella, so I got soaked to the skin.

meanings: it's pouring, it's raining cats and dogs
forms: literally: rain falls, it would kill a mouse

examples.sr: Види какво је време, [па̏да ки̏ша у̀би ми̏ша]!
examples.en: Look at the weather, it's pouring!

note: A rhyming expression for heavy rain.

forms: literally: white lie

examples.sr: Рекла сам [бѐлу ла̑ж] да га не повредим.
examples.en: I told a white lie so as not to hurt him.

meanings: a person who stands out from the others, an odd one out
forms: literally: white crow

examples.en: In this company I'm the odd one out.

forms: literally: black sheep

examples.sr: Од малена је [цр̏на о́вца] у породици.
examples.en: Since childhood he has been the black sheep of the family.

forms: literally: white plague

examples.en: The country is facing a falling birth rate.

meanings: to be pessimistic, to see the dark side
forms: literally: to look black

examples.sr: Не [гле̏да̄ј цр̏но], биће све у реду.
examples.en: Don't be so pessimistic, everything will be fine.

note: The opposite - «гледати бело» - means to stare blankly, not understanding anything.

meanings: a day of bad luck and misfortune; a rainy day
forms: literally: black day

examples.en: You should save for a rainy day.

forms: literally: life crossroads

examples.en: I'm at a crossroads in my life.

key: phr:бити као бадњи дан и божић
forms: literally: to be like Christmas Eve and Christmas

examples.sr: Њих двоје [су ка̏о Ба̑дњи да̑н и Бо̀жић], увек заједно.
examples.en: Those two are inseparable, always together.

note: Бадњи дан is January 6, Божић is January 7, two holidays next to each other. Said of close friends.

meanings: out of turn, cutting in line
forms: literally: over the queue

examples.sr: Извините, могу ли да уђем [пре̏ко ре̑да]?
examples.en: Excuse me, may I go in out of turn?

note: At a clinic: «Само нешто да питам» (I only have a question), «Могу ли ја пре Вас?» (May I go before you?).

meanings: to swing between two extremes, to waver between opposite decisions
forms: literally: to sway between two extremes

examples.sr: Дуго сам се [љу̀љао и̏змеђу две̑ кра́јности].
examples.en: I wavered between the two extremes for a long time.

note: Also used of an unstable situation: «политичка сцена се љуља».

meanings: the Easter greeting; the reply is «Ваистину васкрсе!»
forms: literally: Christ is risen

examples.en: - Christ is risen! - Indeed He is risen!

note: This is the church form with ва-. To simply wish someone a happy Easter, say «Срећан Васкрс!» or «Срећан Ускрс!».

forms: literally: to remain in someone's shadow

examples.sr: Цео живот је [о̀стао у сѐнци] старијег брата.
examples.en: All his life he stayed in his older brother's shadow.

forms: literally: outside it is hell

examples.en: Don't go out, it's hell out there.

note: A colloquial expression about heat.

meanings: out of spite, to spite someone

examples.en: He did it to spite everyone.
He parked there to spite his neighbor.

note: Инат is stubbornness, the urge to do the opposite of what is expected. A very Serbian idea.

forms: literally: to have some luck

examples.en: You're lucky.
She has a talent for singing.

note: имати + genitive: имати среће, дара, разума - with a sense of «possessing» some of it.

meanings: may I join in? (a queue, a game)

examples.sr: [Мо̀гу ли да се уба̀цим?] Нас је четворо.
examples.en: May I join in? There are four of us.

note: In a gym, this is how you ask to share a machine and take turns with someone.

meanings: what do you do (for a living or as a hobby)?

examples.en: What do you do? - I work as a programmer.

note: бавити се + instrumental. Formal: «Чиме се бавите?»

key: phr:драго ми је што смо се упознали

examples.sr: [Дра̑го ми је што̏ смо се упо̀знали.] - Такође.
examples.en: Nice to meet you. - Likewise.

note: The reply is «Такође» (likewise).

meanings: to cope, to manage, to get the better of
forms: literally: to come out at the end

examples.sr: Једва сам [иза̀шао на кра̑ј] са папирима.
examples.en: I barely managed to get through the paperwork.

examples.sr: Не могу да [ѝзађем на кра̑ј] са овом децом.
examples.en: I can't cope with these kids.

note: Usually with «са + instr.»: изаћи на крај са неким/нечим.

meanings: to take a chance, to roll the dice
forms: literally: to throw the die

examples.sr: Одлучио је да [ба̏ци ко̏цку] и отвори радњу.
examples.en: He decided to take a chance and open a shop.

note: Related: «коцка је пала» - the die is cast, the decision is made.

forms: literally: the die has fallen

examples.en: The decision has been made, the die is cast.
See you at eight? - Okay!

examples.sr: Ти плаћаш кафу, а ја колаче. - [Ва́жи].
examples.en: You pay for the coffee and I'll pay for the cakes. - Deal.

note: With «ма» («ма важи») it sounds ironic: yeah, sure, right.

examples.sr: Мораш све да научиш до сутра! - [Ма̏ ва́жи].
examples.en: You have to learn it all by tomorrow! - Yeah, sure.

note: Sarcasm: the speaker has no intention of doing it.

forms: literally: to untie the purse

examples.sr: Дошао је ред да и ти [одрѐшиш ке̏су].
examples.en: Now it's your turn to cough up.

note: A colloquial expression. Similar in meaning: «машити се џепа» - to reach for one's wallet.

meanings: to reach for one's wallet, to pay
forms: literally: to grab one's pocket

examples.en: He was the first to reach for his wallet.
I prefer to pay in cash.
Can you pay by card?

note: Also: «у готовини» - in cash, «картицом» - by card.

examples.en: Slow down, there's a speed bump here.

note: Literally a «lying policeman».

examples.sr: На [кру̏жном то̀ку] скрени на другом излазу.
examples.en: At the roundabout, take the second exit.

examples.sr: Личим не на мајку, [ве̏ћ] на бабу.
examples.en: I look like my grandmother, not my mother.

examples.sr: Не [и̏дем] на посао, већ на састанак.
examples.en: I'm not going to work, but to a meeting.

note: The negation can go before the verb or before the contrasted element.

examples.en: Thank you very much for your help!

note: A polite reply is «молим лепо» (you're welcome).

examples.en: Thanks! - You're welcome.

note: «Молим» alone also covers both «please» and «you're welcome».

forms: literally: I told you nicely

examples.sr: [Ле̑по сам ти ре̏као] да не касниш.
examples.en: I told you not to be late.

note: «Лепо» expresses reproach here: it was said clearly and in a friendly way.

meanings: it looks good on you, it suits you (clothes)
forms: literally: it stands beautifully on you

examples.en: This jacket looks good on you.

forms: literally: dream beautifully

examples.en: Good night, sweet dreams!

examples.sr: [Ле̑по је ви̏дети те] после толико времена.
examples.en: It's nice to see you after such a long time.

note: The polite form: «лепо је видети вас».

meanings: to show off, to put on airs
forms: literally: to make oneself important

examples.en: Why are you putting on airs?
Who's putting on airs here?

note: Said playfully to a shy child who turns away from guests.

forms: literally: to know what you are standing on

examples.sr: Када су цене јасне, [зна̑ш на чѐму си].
examples.en: When the prices are clear, you know where you stand.
I want to know where I stand.

note: About clarity in business and relationships.

examples.en: You're right.
He's not right.

note: Not to be confused with «право» - straight ahead: «иди право».

meanings: to learn by heart, to memorize
forms: literally: to learn onto the mind

examples.en: I don't like to memorize things.

examples.sr: Желим да ми сир буде [у ко̏маду].
examples.en: I want the cheese in one piece.

note: In a shop, you say this if you don't want your cheese or cold cuts sliced.

examples.en: I'd like to order food to go.

note: Pronounced as a single unit.

examples.en: No way! Really?

note: «Ма» strengthens the emotion, «иди» is not about walking here.

meanings: I have a reservation under the name ...

examples.sr: Добар дан, [ѝма̄м резерва̀цију на и̏ме] Петровић.
examples.en: Good afternoon, I have a reservation under the name Petrović.

meanings: may I register? (may I check in?)

examples.sr: Добар дан, [мо̀гу ли да се при̏јавим]?
examples.en: Good afternoon, may I check in?

note: At a hotel: пријава means check-in.

meanings: to be bewildered, to be clueless
forms: literally: fell off a pear tree

examples.sr: Шта гледаш, јеси ли [па̏о с кру̏шке]?
examples.en: What are you staring at, did you just fall out of the sky?

note: Said of someone who is confused or unaware of something obvious.

forms: literally: from the sky and into the ribs

examples.sr: Та вест дошла је [с не̏ба па у рѐбра].
examples.en: That news came out of the blue.

forms: literally: whoever gets to the girl first, she is his girl

examples.sr: Нисам хтео да чекам - [ко̏ пре̏ дѐво̄јци, њѐгова дѐво̄јка].
examples.en: I didn't want to wait: first come, first served.

note: A proverb: the quickest one wins.

forms: literally: just the job

examples.en: Lend you money? Not a chance!

note: A sharp, ironic «no».

meanings: to put in order, to sort out

examples.en: I have to sort out my documents.

forms: literally: when grapes grow on a willow

examples.sr: Он ће вратити дуг [ка̏д на вр̏би ро̏ди гро̑жђе].
examples.en: He will pay back the debt when pigs fly.

meanings: to buy a pig in a poke
forms: literally: to buy a cat in a sack

examples.sr: Не волим да [ку̏пим ма̏чку у џа̏ку].
examples.en: I don't like to buy a pig in a poke.

meanings: to be in the saddle, to be in a winning position
forms: literally: to be on a horse

examples.sr: Сад си [на ко̀њу] - имаш посао и стан.
examples.en: Now you're in a good position: you have a job and an apartment.
The sooner we get home, the better.

note: On its own «што пре» means as soon as possible. Do not confuse with «брже-боље» - in a rush.

forms: literally: faster-better

examples.en: He prepared dinner in a rush.

forms: literally: every honor

examples.en: You passed the exam? Well done!
You're doing great with Serbian!
I'm grateful to you for everything.

note: A woman says «захвална сам ти».

meanings: to drop from exhaustion, to be dead on one's feet
forms: literally: to fall off one's feet

examples.sr: Данас сам [па̏о с но̏гу] од посла.
examples.en: Today I was dead on my feet from work.

note: Much more vivid than the plain «био је уморан».

meanings: it wouldn't even occur to me, no way
forms: literally: it does not fall onto my mind

examples.sr: Да га замолим за опроштај? [Не па̏да ми на па̏ме̄т]!
examples.en: Ask him for forgiveness? It wouldn't even occur to me!

forms: literally: to sleep like a slaughtered one

examples.en: Last night I slept like a log.

forms: literally: to swim in money

examples.sr: Он [пли̏ва у па̏рама] откако је продао фирму.
examples.en: He has been rolling in money since he sold the company.

note: A variant: «купати се у парама».

forms: literally: to turn into an ear

examples.sr: Док прича, ја се [претво̀рим у у̏во].
examples.en: When he talks, I'm all ears.

meanings: to be starving, to die of hunger

examples.en: I can't take it anymore, I'm starving.

note: Colloquial, instead of «гладан сам».

meanings: to wake up from a dream

examples.en: I woke up from a bad dream.
I had a strange dream last night.

note: A variant with a verb: «сањао сам нешто чудно».

examples.en: Help, I can't breathe!
Quick, call an ambulance!
I feel sick, I need a doctor.

note: The thing needed is the subject, the person is in the dative: треба ми лекар, треба ми лек.

examples.en: Grandpa had a heart attack.

meanings: I'd like to make an appointment (for a checkup)

examples.en: I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.

note: закажем - to book a time slot; термин - an appointment time.

meanings: do you have any free appointments?

examples.sr: [Да ли и̏мате сло̀бодне тѐрмине] за четвртак?
examples.en: Do you have any free appointments for Thursday?

meanings: I have a referral to a specialist

examples.en: I have a referral to a specialist.
What time suits you?

note: Often also «које време вам одговара».

examples.en: Thanks, I'm just looking.
May I try this on?

meanings: I'm buying it as a gift

examples.sr: Желим да то упакујете, [ку̀пује̄м на по̏клон].
examples.en: Please wrap it, I'm buying it as a gift.
Do you have anything cheaper?
My change, please.

forms: literally: go anywhere, come home

examples.sr: Путовали смо месец дана, али [сву̀да по̏ђи, ку̏ћи до̀ђи].
examples.en: We traveled for a month, but there's no place like home.

forms: literally: measure three times, cut once

examples.sr: Помисли добро: [три̏ пу̏та ме̏ри, јѐдно̄м се́ци].
examples.en: Think it over: measure twice, cut once.

key: phr:човек се учи док је жив
forms: literally: a person learns as long as he lives

examples.sr: Не стиди се, [чо̀век се у̏чи до̏к је жи̑в].
examples.en: Don't be embarrassed, you live and learn.

examples.sr: Не брини, [сва̏кӣ ло̀нац на̑ђе сво̑ј по̀клопац].
examples.en: Don't worry, every pot finds its lid.

note: About everyone finding a match.

key: phr:јабука не пада далеко од стабла
meanings: the apple doesn't fall far from the tree

examples.sr: Син личи на оца - [ја̏бука не па̏да далѐко од ста̏бла].
examples.en: The son looks like his father - the apple doesn't fall far from the tree.

key: phr:ко другоме јаму копа, сам у њу упада
meanings: whoever digs a pit for others falls into it himself

examples.sr: [Ко̏ дру̏гоме ја̏му ко̏па, сам у њу̑ у̀пада].
examples.en: Whoever digs a pit for others falls into it himself.

key: phr:што посејеш, то ћеш и пожњети

examples.en: You reap what you sow.

meanings: the less you know, the better you sleep

examples.en: The less you know, the better you sleep.

key: phr:пала му је секира у мед
meanings: to strike it lucky, to have a stroke of luck
forms: literally: his axe fell into honey

examples.sr: Добио је посао - [па̏ла му је сѐкира у ме̑д].
examples.en: He got the job - he struck it lucky.

key: phr:вук длаку мења, али ћуд никада
meanings: a leopard can't change its spots
forms: literally: the wolf changes its coat, but never its nature

examples.sr: [Ву̑к дла̏ку ме̏ња, а̏ли ћу̑д ни̏када] - није се променио.
examples.en: A leopard can't change its spots - he hasn't changed.

note: The point: a person does not change at heart.

forms: literally: like a cat around hot porridge

examples.sr: Он се врти [ка̏о ма̏чка о̏ко врѐле ка̏ше].
examples.en: He keeps beating around the bush.

key: phr:ко зна зашто је то добро
meanings: every cloud has a silver lining, a blessing in disguise
forms: literally: who knows why it is good

examples.sr: Изгубио је посао, али [ко̏ зна̑ за̏што је то̑ до̀бро].
examples.en: He lost his job, but who knows, it may be a blessing in disguise.
Which Slava do you celebrate?

note: A question about which saint the family honors on that day.

forms: literally: may they live

examples.en: Cheers! - Cheers!
Hi, what's up?

note: A casual alternative to «како си».

meanings: who cares about you, nobody pays any attention to you

examples.sr: Он хоће да се прави важан, али [ко̏ га ши̏ша].
examples.en: He wants to act important, but who cares about him?

note: Colloquial, a bit rude: said of someone nobody notices or listens to.

forms: literally: there is no connection

examples.en: I'm late. - Never mind.

meanings: what's wrong with you?, what's your problem?

examples.en: Why are you so quiet? What's wrong with you?

note: Colloquial: asks for the reason behind someone's behavior.

forms: literally: there is no chance

examples.sr: Да ћу ја то урадити? [Не̑ма ша̏нсе].
examples.en: Me, do that? No way.

key: phr:то ти је што ти је

examples.sr: Тако је како је, [то̑ ти је што̏ ти је].
examples.en: That's how it is, it is what it is.

note: Accepting a situation that cannot be changed.

meanings: not really in the mood, not really my thing

examples.sr: Данас [ни́сам ба̏ш у фа̏зону] за излазак.
examples.en: I'm not really in the mood to go out today.

note: Colloquial «фазон» - a state of mind, a mood.

examples.sr: Ја сам рекао своје, [ра̏ди ка̏ко зна̑ш и у̀ме̄ш].
examples.en: I've said my piece, do as you see fit.

meanings: oh, come on, the things you hear

examples.sr: Рекао је да не пије? [Е̏х, сва̏шта].
examples.en: He said he doesn't drink? Oh, come on.

note: Disbelief or surprise.

forms: literally: necessary evil

examples.en: Taxes are a necessary evil.

meanings: to win, to take the prize
forms: literally: to carry off the cord

examples.sr: Наш тим је [по̏нео шну̑р] у финалу.
examples.en: Our team won the final.

meanings: a pretentious upstart who puts on airs
forms: literally: a pumpkin that puts on airs

examples.en: That man is a real conceited upstart.

note: Said of someone who has recently become rich and puts on airs.

forms: literally: wipe!

examples.en: Get lost!

note: Rude: an order to leave.

examples.sr: У њеном стану је [ка̏о у апоте́ци].
examples.en: Her apartment is spotless.

forms: literally: it was before Christ

examples.en: That was ages ago, before Christ.

meanings: in the middle of nowhere, very far away

examples.en: We live in the middle of nowhere.

note: Literally «behind God's back». A variant: «Богу иза ногу».

forms: literally: to not close one's mouth

examples.en: She hasn't stopped talking since morning.

forms: literally: so that you lick your fingers

examples.en: This baklava is finger-licking good.

note: Colloquially: «боли глава» - mind-blowingly delicious.

examples.en: First of all, thank you for the invitation.

examples.sr: [По мо̑м ми̏шљењу], то је добра идеја.
examples.en: In my opinion, it's a good idea.
Sorry, but I disagree.

meanings: that makes no sense, there's no point

examples.en: There's no point, you have to decide.
Let me explain what happened.

examples.sr: [Мо̀жда се ни̏када не̑ће̄мо сло̀жити], али то је у реду.
examples.en: Maybe we'll never agree, but that's okay.

forms: literally: my ear hurts

examples.en: What are they saying? I couldn't care less.

note: «Баш ме брига» - the same, but ruder.

examples.en: Look at the room, it's like a pigsty!

forms: literally: poor as a church mouse

examples.en: He's poor as a church mouse.

forms: literally: when Karađorđe is born

examples.sr: Он ће платити [ка̏д се ро̏ди Карађо̀рђе].
examples.en: He'll pay when hell freezes over.

forms: literally: in the cuckoo's summer

examples.en: He'll pay the debt back on the twelfth of never.

key: phr:не зна се ко пије, а ко плаћа
meanings: total chaos, nobody knows what is going on
forms: literally: nobody knows who is drinking and who is paying

examples.sr: На састанку [се не зна̑ ко̏ пи̏је̄, а ко̏ пла́ћа].
examples.en: The meeting was total chaos.

forms: literally: I have boiled

examples.sr: Напољу је четрдесет степени, [ску̏вао сам се].
examples.en: It's 40 degrees Celsius outside, I'm boiling.
Without a jacket I'm freezing.

meanings: to give up the ghost, to pass away
forms: literally: to let out one's soul

examples.en: Grandpa passed away in his sleep.

forms: literally: to stretch out one's hooves

examples.en: The old cow kicked the bucket.

note: Colloquial and jocular.

meanings: to live in clover, to live in luxury
forms: literally: lives like a kidney in suet

examples.en: He lives in clover.

meanings: you shouldn't have gone to the trouble

examples.sr: Тако леп поклон! [Нѝје тре̏бало да се му̏чиш].
examples.en: Such a lovely gift! You shouldn't have.

note: The polite form: «није требало да се мучите».

examples.sr: [Ба̏ш ле̑по од те̏бе] што си дошао.
examples.en: It's really nice of you to have come.

meanings: I have a little surprise for you

examples.en: I have a little surprise for you.

meanings: to play dumb, to pretend not to understand
forms: literally: to pretend to be an Englishman

examples.sr: Не [пра̏ви се Ѐнгле̄з], добро знаш о чему се ради.
examples.en: Don't play dumb, you know exactly what this is about.

meanings: to not mince words, to speak frankly
forms: literally: to have no hair on one's tongue

examples.en: He doesn't mince words.

meanings: to idle, to goof off, to gawk around
forms: literally: to catch yawns

examples.en: Don't just stand around gawking, do something.

meanings: to give a boost, to encourage, to support
forms: literally: to give a wind in the back

examples.sr: Хвала што ми дајеш [ве̏тар у ле́ђа].
examples.en: Thanks for giving me a boost.

forms: literally: to drink like a snake

examples.en: He drinks like a fish.

key: phr:ко се мача лати, од мача ће и погинути
meanings: he who lives by the sword dies by the sword

examples.sr: [Ко̏ се ма̏ча ла̏ти, од ма̏ча ће и по̀гинути].
examples.en: He who lives by the sword dies by the sword.

meanings: to make a mountain out of a molehill

examples.en: Don't make a mountain out of a molehill.

meanings: to have a guilty conscience, to have something to hide
forms: literally: to have butter on one's head

examples.sr: Он [и̏ма пу̏тер на гла́ви], зато ћути.
examples.en: He has a guilty conscience, which is why he's keeping quiet.

examples.sr: [Сре̏ћна Но̑ва го̏дина]! Нека ти донесе много среће.
examples.en: Happy New Year! May it bring you lots of luck.

key: phr:нека ти донесе много среће, здравља и љубави
meanings: may it bring you lots of luck, health and love

examples.sr: Срећна Нова година! [Не̏ка ти до̀несе мно̏го сре̏ће, здра̏вља и љу́бави].
examples.en: Happy New Year! May it bring you lots of luck, health and love.

forms: literally: without three fingers there is no cross

examples.sr: Попиј и трећу, [без три̏ пр̏ста не̑ма кр̏ста].
examples.en: Have a third one too, third time's the charm.

note: In Serbia coffee is brought to a boil three times; the saying alludes to crossing oneself with three fingers.

meanings: Truly He is born! (the reply to the Christmas greeting)

examples.en: - Christ is born! - Truly He is born!
I'm sending my friends a card: Merry Christmas!

note: Christmas in Serbia is on January 7.

examples.en: We wished our neighbors a happy Christmas Eve!

note: Christmas Eve is on January 6.

examples.en: I overate today.

forms: literally: wooden lawyer

examples.en: What, are you his self-appointed lawyer?

note: Someone who stands up for another person without being asked.

forms: literally: mad as electric current

examples.en: He's totally nuts.

forms: literally: to work with full steam

examples.en: The factory is working at full steam.

examples.sr: Да је он отишао? [Пр̀ви пу̑т чу̏је̄м].
examples.en: He left? That's news to me.
I was late. - So what?

meanings: I was just thinking about that

examples.sr: [Та́ма̄н сам ми̏слио на то̑], зови га.
examples.en: I was just thinking about that, call him.

meanings: all that glitters is not gold

examples.en: Be careful, all that glitters is not gold.

key: phr:ко се последњи смеје, најслађе се смеје
meanings: he who laughs last laughs best
forms: literally: whoever laughs last laughs the sweetest

examples.sr: [Ко̏ се по̀следњӣ смѐје̄, на̏јслађе се смѐје̄].
examples.en: He who laughs last laughs best.

meanings: same as ever, the same old

examples.en: What's new? - Same as ever.

meanings: to look back on the past year

examples.sr: Пред Нову годину [о̀сврнемо се на про̀теклу го̀дину].
examples.en: Before New Year we look back on the past year.

meanings: I don't care about that, it's not important to me

examples.sr: Резултат ме не занима, [нѝје ми ста̏ло до то́га].
examples.en: The result doesn't interest me, I don't care about it.

note: «стало ми је до + gen.» - something matters to me, I care about it.

examples.en: I can't stand this food.

note: Stronger: «апсолутно не подносим».

examples.en: I love going to visit people.

forms: literally: black wine

examples.en: We'll order a bottle of red wine.

note: The grapes are dark, so red wine is called «black» in Serbian. White wine is «бело вино».

examples.sr: Падала је киша, [та̀ко̄ да] нисмо ишли у парк.
examples.en: It was raining, so we didn't go to the park.

note: A conjunction of result: the main clause comes first, then the result.

examples.sr: Он је постао директор? [Ко̏ би ре̏као]!
examples.en: He became a director? Who would have thought!
I heard that you're moving.

forms: literally: to look for a hair in an egg

examples.en: He's always nitpicking.

meanings: I don't get the joke, I don't see the point

examples.en: What are they laughing at? I don't get the joke.

note: A meme with Saša Matić, a blind singer.

meanings: to see through a trick, to catch on to someone's game
forms: literally: to break through the trick

examples.en: I've seen through your trick.

forms: literally: relaxed

examples.en: Sorry for being late. - No worries.

meanings: pretty please (a request among close people)
forms: literally: I kiss you

examples.en: Open the window, pretty please!
Kisses, bye!

note: Only for warm relationships; with strangers say «молим вас».

examples.en: Please cut my hair shorter.
Please give me bangs.
Cook it on low heat.

forms: literally: there is no panic

examples.en: - Sorry I'm late. - No worries.
No worries, we'll make it on time.

note: Colloquial slang. Close in meaning: «није фрка» - no big deal.

forms: literally: if it is not a panic for you

examples.sr: [А̏ко ти нѝје фр̏ка], помози ми са торбама.
examples.en: If it's no trouble, help me with the bags.

examples.sr: - Можеш ли да ме одвезеш? - [Нѝје ми фр̏ка].
examples.en: - Can you give me a ride? - No trouble.

note: An informal polite request; the reply is «није ми фрка» - no trouble for me.

meanings: get lost, get out of here
forms: literally: carry yourself off

examples.en: Get out of here!
I told him to get lost.

note: Colloquial and rude; strengthened with «бре»: «носи се, бре!».

examples.en: They say ironically: the further south, the sadder.

examples.sr: Плате су све ниже, [што̏ ју̏жније, то̑ ту̏жније].
examples.en: Wages keep getting lower: the further south, the sadder.

note: A joking saying about a hard economic situation; it rhymes: «јужније - тужније».

key: phr:мени је милије поред мога илије
meanings: I'd rather be beside my beloved than in luxury
forms: literally: I like it better beside my Ilija

examples.sr: Не треба ми палата, [ме̏ни је ми̏лије по̏ред мо̑га Ѝлије].
examples.en: I don't need a palace, I'm happiest by my Ilija's side.

examples.sr: Могла би у град, али [ме̏ни је ми̏лије по̏ред мо̑га Ѝлије].
examples.en: I could move to the city, but I'm happiest by my Ilija's side.

note: A rhyming proverb (милије - Илије): being near a loved one beats any comfort.

examples.en: He decided to grow a beard.
He grew a beard in the winter.

meanings: leave me alone; also let go of me, let me through

examples.en: Please, leave me in peace.
Oh, forget him, he's crazy!

note: The sense depends on the situation: let go, let me through, leave alone, never mind. Example: «пусти ме да радим шта хоћу» - let me do what I want.

forms: literally: to let out a rumor

examples.sr: Неко је [пу̏стио ру̏жне гла̀сине] о њој.
examples.en: Someone spread nasty rumors about her.
Don't spread rumors without proof.

forms: literally: in love up to the ears

examples.sr: Он је [за̀љубљен до у̀шијӯ] у њу.
examples.en: He's head over heels in love with her.
I'm head over heels in love with you.

examples.sr: [О̀сећам не̏што пре̏ма те̏би], али се плашим да кажем.
examples.en: I have feelings for you, but I'm afraid to say so.
I know you have feelings for me.

examples.sr: Знам да [ти си мо̀ја дру̏га поло̀вина].
examples.en: I know that you are my other half.
For him she is the other half.

note: A man can say jokingly to a woman: «ти си моја лепша половина» - you are my better half.

meanings: I like you, I'm into you

examples.sr: [Сви̏ђаш ми се] више него што мислиш.
examples.en: I like you more than you think.
I really like you.

note: «Свиђати се» takes the dative: «ти ми се свиђаш», «свиђам му се» - he likes me.
